marks.gloss_en: מנלן? אתיא כתיבה כתיבה: כתיב הכא 'ותכתב אסתר המלכה' (Esther 9:29), וכתיב התם 'ואני כותב על הספר בדיו' (Jer 36:18)
דכתיב ככתבם וכזמנם -- the verse adduced for the mishnah's requirement of Ashurit
the stam: as it is written, 'according to their writing and according to their time' (Esther 9:27)
the mishnah: R' Meir -- one must read all of it
the baraita: R' Shimon ben Yochai -- from 'On that night' (Esther 6:1)
the mishnah: a townsman who went to a walled city, or a city-man who went to a town -- if he is destined to return to his place, he reads as his place does
kankantom is charta de'ushkafei (the shoemakers' black)
R' Yochanan: all of them expounded one verse -- 'and Esther the queen and Mordechai the Jew wrote all the power' (Esther 9:29)
per the one who says 'from "a certain Jew"': the power of Mordechai
Rav Huna: [they derived it] from here -- 'and what they saw concerning this, and what had come upon them' (Esther 9:26)

per 'all of it': what Achashverosh saw, that he used the Temple vessels; 'concerning this' -- because he counted seventy years and they were not redeemed; 'what had come upon them' -- that he killed Vashti
per 'from "a certain Jew"': what Mordechai saw, that he was zealous against Haman; 'concerning this' -- that Haman made himself an idol; 'what had come upon them' -- that a miracle occurred

per 'from "after these things"': what Haman saw, that he grew zealous against all the Jews; 'concerning this' -- because Mordechai would not bow or prostrate himself; 'what had come upon them' -- 'and they hanged him and his sons on the gallows'
per 'from "on that night"': what Achashverosh saw, to bring the book of chronicles; 'concerning this' -- that Esther had invited Haman with him; 'what had come upon them' -- that a miracle occurred
Rav: the halakha follows the one who says [the Megilla is read] in its entirety
Rav: the Megilla is called a 'book', and it is called a 'letter'
one who reads from a Megilla written among the Writings has not fulfilled [his obligation]
Levi bar Shmuel was reading before Rav Yehuda from a Megilla written among the Writings
אשכחן פרוז, מוקף מנא לן? סברא הוא: מדפרוז בן יומו קרוי פרוז, מוקף בן יומו קרוי מוקף
the stam: it is reasoning -- since a one-day paruz is called paruz, a one-day mukaf is called mukaf
מאי טעמא? האי כבני העיר בעי למיקרי, ורבנן הוא דאקילו על הכפרים ... הני מילי כי איתיה בדוכתיה, אבל כי איתיה בעיר כבני עיר בעי למיקרי
Rava: a villager who went to a town reads with them either way [whether or not he will return]
איתיביה אביי: בן כרך שהלך לעיר בין כך ובין כך קורא כמקומו -- read (אלא לאו) as 'a villager', the baraita has the villager in a town read as his village, against Rava
the baraita as cited: a city-man who went to a town reads as his own place either way
ולאו תרוצי מתרצת? תני: קורא עמהן -- since the baraita must be emended in any case, emend it to 'he reads with them' (= p_tni_korei_imahem)
the stam: have you not emended it anyway? teach [instead]: he reads with them
Rava: the mishnah's 'destined to return' was taught only of one destined to return on the night of the fourteenth
